## Summary

The degradation is latency, not failures. One fault, in `ts-route-service`, adds a fixed ~1.5 s delay to every `GET /api/v1/routeservice/routes/{routeId}` call. That delay propagates through the services that call it, so user-facing travel, preserve, food and route-plan requests take 1.5 s to 15 s. I found one root cause and no independent second fault.

## Affected endpoints (abnormal vs normal, server spans)

| Endpoint (service) | Normal p95 | Abnormal p95 / typical |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/v1/admintravelservice/admintravel (ts-admin-travel-service) | ~62 ms | ~15.2 s (every call) |
| GET /api/v1/travelservice/admin_trip, travel2service/admin_trip | ~46–49 ms | ~7.6 s (every call) |
| POST /api/v1/preserveservice/preserve (ts-preserve-service) | ~137 ms | ~3.1 s (every call) |
| POST /travelPlan/minStation (ts-travel-plan / ts-route-plan) | ~105–115 ms | ~1.6–3.1 s |
| POST /travelPlan/quickest and /cheapest | ~113–120 ms | ~1.6 s |
| POST /trip_detail (ts-travel-service) | — | ~1.55 s |
| GET /foodservice/foods/... (ts-food-service) | ~30 ms | ~1.54 s |

The latencies cluster at multiples of about 1.5 s: one slow call is 1.5 s, two are 3 s, five are 7.5 s, and ten are 15 s. That pattern points to a sequential fan-out over a single slow dependency.

## Root cause: ts-route-service, `RouteController.queryById`

- `GET /api/v1/routeservice/routes/{routeId}` takes 1511–1518 ms on every call in abnormal data, against about 1.8 ms in normal data (n=179 vs 787). The spread is tight, with min ≈ max ≈ 1.5 s.
- The child `RouteRepository.findById` and the SQL spans take under 1 ms. The 1.5 s is spent inside the controller method itself, outside the database.
- All of this is on one pod, `ts-route-service-5b769949fc-mbhns` in namespace `ts12`.
- Other `ts-route-service` endpoints are only slightly slower (`/routes` p50 11 ms vs 8 ms; `/routes/{start}/{end}` 6.8 ms vs 5.0 ms). The fault is specific to the by-id handler.
- Route-service pod CPU time rose slightly (70.8 s vs 57.4 s), and network IO also rose. The fixed floor is consistent with an injected sleep, a blocking wait, or a timeout/retry loop inside the handler. The telemetry does not say which mechanism.

## Propagation path

The by-id span is called by these services, measured in abnormal traces:

- `ts-travel-service` (55 calls) and `ts-travel2-service` (43) run `admin_trip` by calling route-service several times in sequence. This gives roughly 7.6 s on `admin_trip` and roughly 15.2 s on `admintravel` (ts-admin-travel-service calls it twice).
- `ts-basic-service` (20 calls) is the hub for preserve and travel-plan. Its p95 went from about 20 ms to 1.53 s, while its p50 stayed at about 12 ms. Preserve takes about 3.1 s.
- `ts-route-plan-service` (2 calls) feeds minStopStations and travel-plan, giving p95 of about 1.6 s.
- `ts-food-service` also picks up one 1.5 s call per request.

Services not on this chain show no latency change: auth, user, order, order-other, seat, station, train, price, config, contacts, verification-code, and inside-payment. The `ts-route-service` error logs ("Route not found") appear in normal data too and are not the cause.

## Other findings

- No 5xx responses were observed anywhere. Abnormal and normal traces show the same small background error counts, mostly from the loadgenerator. This is a latency incident.
- Logs contain no message naming the cause of the 1.5 s delay. The WARNs about "No Content" from travel-plan and the "Cookie not found" WARNs from verification-code are downstream or unrelated noise.

## Confidence and gaps

- High confidence that the delay sits in `ts-route-service`'s by-id handler on pod `ts-route-service-5b769949fc-mbhns`, and that it explains every slow endpoint.
- The exact mechanism inside `queryById` is not visible in the telemetry. Source code or a thread dump of that pod would be needed to tell whether it is an injected sleep, a lock, or a retry loop.
